findings.summary: Brisling has higher WER than Greedy-CTC (6.4% vs 8.9%) but lower median latency (41 ms vs 22 ms).
findings.scope: Brindle-Voice test set, batch size 1, fp16, Corvex A2, Lumen 3.1
findings.caveats: No statistical tests reported; single test set; latency is median over 2,000 utterances.

sentences.text: On the Brindle-Voice test set, Brisling achieved a lower median latency than Talmar (41 ms vs 118 ms per utterance) but a slightly higher WER (6.4% vs 6.1%).
This latency advantage was accompanied by a substantially lower number of decoder passes (4.0 vs 37.6 per utterance).
Relative to the Greedy-CTC reference, Brisling reduced WER (6.4% vs 8.9%) at the cost of higher median latency (41 ms vs 22 ms).
